protocols.name: Train on MS MARCO; evaluate zero-shot on BEIR
protocols.detail: Train dense retrievers on MS MARCO and report zero-shot effectiveness across BEIR datasets; no BEIR tuning.
evidence: Cluster-based Partial Dense Retrieval Fused with Sparse Text Retrieval
Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

protocols.name: ODQA training on NQ with multi-dataset evaluation
protocols.detail: Train on NQ and report Acc@20/100 (or Recall@k) on NQ, SQuAD, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, CuratedTREC using a fixed Wikipedia passage index.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

protocols.name: BM25 candidate generation then neural reranking
protocols.detail: Generate top-k (e.g., k=100–150) candidates with BM25 (or QL) and rerank with neural models; select k on dev; report P@20/nDCG@20/ERR@20.
evidence: CEDR

protocols.name: Per-language BM25 tuning for multilingual retrieval
protocols.detail: Grid-search BM25 k,b on a per-language dev set to optimize MRR@100, then test on Mr.TyDi.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

protocols.name: Sparse–Dense hybrid score fusion
protocols.detail: Normalize BM25 and dense scores to [0,1] and combine via s_sparse + α·s_dense; tune α on dev.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

protocols.name: Dense ANN search configuration
protocols.detail: Use Faiss FlatIP (inner-product) indexes for dense retrieval; evaluate MRR/Recall at cutoffs like 100.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

protocols.name: Retrieval granularity comparisons under equal budgets
protocols.detail: Index at passage/sentence/proposition granularities; map fine units back to passages and constrain input to equal token budgets for downstream LMs.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

protocols.name: Retrieval-augmented generation with capped context
protocols.detail: Feed top-retrieved context to an LM with fixed token cap (e.g., 100 or 500 tokens) and report EM@token-budget alongside closed-book EM.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

protocols.name: Report effectiveness–efficiency trade-offs
protocols.detail: Alongside effectiveness, report index size and per-query latency/CPU-time; analyze scaling with method knobs (e.g., clusters).
evidence: Cluster-based Partial Dense Retrieval Fused with Sparse Text Retrieval
Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

protocols.name: Held-out validation and cross-year/fold splits
protocols.detail: Use fixed folds (e.g., Robust04 5-fold) or year-held-out splits (WebTrack) to tune hyperparameters and select checkpoints.
evidence: CEDR

protocols.name: Statistical significance testing
protocols.detail: Use paired tests across queries/topics (e.g., paired t-test) when claiming improvements.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

protocols.name: Recall vs ranking-error decomposition
protocols.detail: Break down MRR into retrieval failures (Recall@k) vs ranking quality conditional on at-least-one relevant retrieved.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

protocols.name: Rank list overlap analysis
protocols.detail: Compute Rank Biased Overlap between methods to assess lexical vs semantic behavior similarities.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

protocols.name: Query stress tests
protocols.detail: Evaluate on token-shuffled queries to probe order sensitivity and lexical matching behavior.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

protocols.name: Generated context quality checks
protocols.detail: Manually annotate a sample of generated propositions for faithfulness/minimality/stand-alone properties and report error rates.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

controls.name: Strong lexical baseline (BM25) with and without tuning
controls.detail: Evaluate BM25 with default settings and after per-dataset/per-language k,b tuning on dev.
controls.rules_out: that improvements stem from weak or untuned sparse baselines rather than the proposed method.
evidence: CEDR
Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval
Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

controls.name: Sparse-only vs dense-only vs hybrid ablations
controls.detail: Compare standalone sparse and dense retrievers to their (score-level or vector-level) hybrid under identical candidate pools and tuning budgets.
controls.rules_out: that gains are merely inherited from one component rather than true complementarity or the proposed integration.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval
Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

controls.name: Equal token-budget constraint
controls.detail: Fix the total number of input tokens supplied to downstream LMs across retrieval granularities/indices.
controls.rules_out: that differences are due to unequal context sizes rather than retrieval granularity or representation.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

controls.name: Closed-book (no retrieval) baseline
controls.detail: Evaluate the LM without any retrieved context under the same prompting/inference setup.
controls.rules_out: that improvements come from the language model’s internal knowledge rather than retrieval.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

controls.name: Supervised vs unsupervised retriever variants
controls.detail: Evaluate both supervised (e.g., DPR/GTR) and unsupervised (e.g., Contriever/SimCSE) retrievers under the same indexing and evaluation pipelines.
controls.rules_out: that effects are artifacts of supervision/training-data overlap rather than the experimental factor (e.g., granularity).
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

controls.name: Dimension-matched ensemble baseline
controls.detail: Concatenate two independently trained dense retrievers to match the proposed concatenated embedding dimensionality.
controls.rules_out: that improvements arise from larger vector dimensionality/parameter count rather than the specific integration.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

controls.name: Contextualization controls (GloVe/ELMo/VanillaBERT/non-joint)
controls.detail: Swap contextual backbones or remove joint mechanisms (e.g., [CLS] fusion) while keeping the reranker architecture and training identical.
controls.rules_out: that gains are solely from using any contextual LM or fine-tuning classifier rather than the proposed ranking integration.
evidence: CEDR

controls.name: Add sparse retriever at inference
controls.detail: Augment the proposed dense method with BM25 at inference and measure incremental gains.
controls.rules_out: that reported gains already rely on having sparse access at inference rather than learning sparse-like signals.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

controls.name: Token-order shuffle control
controls.detail: Evaluate with randomly shuffled query tokens.
controls.rules_out: that improvements depend on order-sensitive semantics rather than robust lexical/term-matching behavior.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

confounds.name: Incomplete relevance judgments (unjudged treated as non-relevant)
confounds.detail: Sparse pooling leads to false negatives that can distort Recall/MRR comparisons, especially across methods with different candidate distributions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Acknowledge judgment incompleteness; where possible, compare relative trends and complement with recall@k and conditional ranking analyses; use paired tests across identical pools.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

confounds.name: Low MRR due to retrieval failure (not ranking)
confounds.detail: A model may have poor MRR because it misses any relevant item, not because it ranks retrieved relevant items poorly.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report Recall@k and the distribution of ranks conditional on at-least-one relevant retrieved to separate failure modes.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

confounds.name: Training/test overlap or supervised-data bias
confounds.detail: Supervised retrievers may benefit from overlap or bias toward training formats/domains, inflating gains unrelated to the tested factor.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report supervised vs unsupervised retrievers separately; flag datasets seen during training; highlight where gains persist or increase on unseen datasets.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

confounds.name: Token-density advantage (context packing)
confounds.detail: Apparent gains from finer-grained units may result from packing more answer-bearing tokens per budget rather than better semantics.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Match token budgets and measure gold-answer recall as a function of retrieved-word count across indices.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

confounds.name: Improvement due to larger embedding dimensionality
confounds.detail: Concatenation-based methods may win because of increased vector size/parameters, not better modeling.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare against size-matched ensembles (e.g., concatenating two independent retrievers) and show they underperform the proposed integration.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

confounds.name: Gains rely on sparse access at inference
confounds.detail: If the method implicitly uses or is complemented by sparse retrieval at inference, improvements may not reflect learned signals.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Add BM25 at inference to the proposed method; minimal additional gain indicates the method already captures sparse-like cues.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

confounds.name: Lexical vs semantic explanation
confounds.detail: Improvements could be from lexical matching rather than improved semantic retrieval (or vice versa).
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compute RBO overlap with BM25 and run token-shuffled query tests to diagnose lexical matching behavior.
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?

confounds.name: Attribution to fine-tuning alone (not architecture)
confounds.detail: Observed gains may be due solely to LM fine-tuning or [CLS] classification rather than the ranking integration.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare non-joint contextual baselines and VanillaBERT classifier to the joint integration; show additional gains from the proposed mechanism.
evidence: CEDR

confounds.name: Impractical inference speed
confounds.detail: Benefits may vanish under realistic latency constraints.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure throughput/latency and show competitive performance with truncated/backbone-layer limits.
evidence: CEDR

confounds.name: Random variation/sampling noise
confounds.detail: Observed improvements may be due to chance given dataset splits and query sets.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use paired statistical tests (e.g., paired t-test) across queries/topics to establish significance.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

confounds.name: Domain/language mismatch for dense retrievers
confounds.detail: Zero-shot underperformance can be due to training on different domains/languages rather than method limitations.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Prefer in-domain multilingual training or explicitly note limitations; qualitative analysis and preliminary fine-tuning evidence where available.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

confounds.name: Unequal context across conditions
confounds.detail: Different amounts of retrieved text given to the LM can confound downstream comparisons.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Fix token budgets across conditions when evaluating retrieval granularity/RAG.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

confounds.name: LM internal knowledge explains RAG gains
confounds.detail: Improvements may come from the LM’s parametric memory rather than retrieval.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Include closed-book baselines under the same prompting to isolate retrieval effects.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

confounds.name: BM25 parameterization explains differences
confounds.detail: Poorly tuned sparse baselines can make dense or hybrid methods look better.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Per-language/per-dataset BM25 grid search on dev; compare against tuned BM25.
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval

confounds.name: Benefits limited to frequent/head entities
confounds.detail: Apparent gains may accrue only for common entities, not the long tail.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Analyze performance as a function of entity frequency estimated from a large BM25 retrieval set.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

confounds.name: Low-quality generated propositions
confounds.detail: Unfaithful/non-minimal propositions can artifactually affect retrieval outcomes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Manual proposition quality audits with error categorization and rates.
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

controls.rules_out: that improvements come from the language model’s internal knowledge rather than retrieval.

controls.name: Contextualization controls
evidence: CEDR
controls.detail: Swap contextual backbones or remove joint mechanisms (e.g., [CLS] fusion) while keeping the reranker architecture and training identical.
controls.rules_out: that gains are solely from using any contextual LM or fine-tuning classifier rather than the proposed ranking integration.

controls.name: Dimension-matched ensemble baseline
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?
controls.detail: Concatenate two independently trained dense retrievers to match the proposed concatenated embedding dimensionality.
controls.rules_out: that improvements arise from larger vector dimensionality/parameter count rather than the specific integration.

controls.name: Equal token-budget constraint
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
controls.detail: Fix the total number of input tokens supplied to downstream LMs across retrieval granularities/indices.
controls.rules_out: that differences are due to unequal context sizes rather than retrieval granularity or representation.

controls.name: Supervised vs unsupervised retriever variants
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
controls.detail: Evaluate both supervised (e.g., DPR/GTR) and unsupervised (e.g., Contriever/SimCSE) retrievers under the same indexing and evaluation pipelines.
controls.rules_out: that effects are artifacts of supervision/training-data overlap rather than the experimental factor (e.g., granularity).

controls.name: Token-order shuffle control
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?
controls.detail: Evaluate with randomly shuffled query tokens.
controls.rules_out: that improvements depend on order-sensitive semantics rather than robust lexical/term-matching behavior.

confounds.name: Attribution to fine-tuning alone
evidence: CEDR
confounds.detail: Observed gains may be due solely to LM fine-tuning or [CLS] classification rather than the ranking integration.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare non-joint contextual baselines and VanillaBERT classifier to the joint integration; show additional gains from the proposed mechanism.

confounds.name: BM25 parameterization explains differences
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval
confounds.detail: Poorly tuned sparse baselines can make dense or hybrid methods look better.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Per-language/per-dataset BM25 grid search on dev; compare against tuned BM25.

confounds.name: Benefits limited to frequent/head entities
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
confounds.detail: Apparent gains may accrue only for common entities, not the long tail.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Analyze performance as a function of entity frequency estimated from a large BM25 retrieval set.

confounds.name: Domain/language mismatch for dense retrievers
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval
confounds.detail: Zero-shot underperformance can be due to training on different domains/languages rather than method limitations.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Prefer in-domain multilingual training or explicitly note limitations; qualitative analysis and preliminary fine-tuning evidence where available.

confounds.name: Gains rely on sparse access at inference
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?
confounds.detail: If the method implicitly uses or is complemented by sparse retrieval at inference, improvements may not reflect learned signals.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Add BM25 at inference to the proposed method; minimal additional gain indicates the method already captures sparse-like cues.

confounds.name: Impractical inference speed
evidence: CEDR
confounds.detail: Benefits may vanish under realistic latency constraints.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure throughput/latency and show competitive performance with truncated/backbone-layer limits.

confounds.name: Improvement due to larger embedding dimensionality
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?
confounds.detail: Concatenation-based methods may win because of increased vector size/parameters, not better modeling.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare against size-matched ensembles (e.g., concatenating two independent retrievers) and show they underperform the proposed integration.

confounds.name: Incomplete relevance judgments
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval
variants: Incomplete relevance judgments (unjudged treated as non-relevant)
confounds.detail: Sparse pooling leads to false negatives that can distort Recall/MRR comparisons, especially across methods with different candidate distributions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Acknowledge judgment incompleteness; where possible, compare relative trends and complement with recall@k and conditional ranking analyses; use paired tests across identical pools.

confounds.name: LM internal knowledge explains RAG gains
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
confounds.detail: Improvements may come from the LM’s parametric memory rather than retrieval.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Include closed-book baselines under the same prompting to isolate retrieval effects.

confounds.name: Lexical vs semantic explanation
evidence: Salient Phrase Aware Dense Retrieval: Can a Dense Retriever Imitate a Sparse One?
confounds.detail: Improvements could be from lexical matching rather than improved semantic retrieval (or vice versa).
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compute RBO overlap with BM25 and run token-shuffled query tests to diagnose lexical matching behavior.

confounds.name: Low MRR due to retrieval failure
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval
variants: Low MRR due to retrieval failure (not ranking)
confounds.detail: A model may have poor MRR because it misses any relevant item, not because it ranks retrieved relevant items poorly.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report Recall@k and the distribution of ranks conditional on at-least-one relevant retrieved to separate failure modes.

confounds.name: Low-quality generated propositions
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
confounds.detail: Unfaithful/non-minimal propositions can artifactually affect retrieval outcomes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Manual proposition quality audits with error categorization and rates.

confounds.name: Random variation/sampling noise
evidence: Mr. TyDi: A Multi-lingual Benchmark for Dense Retrieval
confounds.detail: Observed improvements may be due to chance given dataset splits and query sets.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use paired statistical tests (e.g., paired t-test) across queries/topics to establish significance.

confounds.name: Token-density advantage
evidence: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
confounds.detail: Apparent gains from finer-grained units may result from packing more answer-bearing tokens per budget rather than better semantics.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Match token budgets and measure gold-answer recall as a function of retrieved-word count across indices.

experiment_recipes.goal: Zero-shot BEIR after MS MARCO training gate
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Train on MS MARCO; evaluate zero-shot on BEIR — Train dense retrievers on MS MARCO and report zero-shot effectiveness across BEIR datasets; no BEIR tuning.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if (a) training data sources == {MS MARCO (train)} and tuned_on ∩ {BEIR datasets} == ∅; (b) number of BEIR datasets evaluated ≥ 8; (c) for each evaluated BEIR dataset, both nDCG@20 and Recall@100 are reported. Otherwise fail.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Verifies the zero-shot evaluation norm on BEIR after MS MARCO training with required coverage and metrics.

experiment_recipes.goal: Tuned BM25 apparatus on BEIR dev/test
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Per-language BM25 tuning for multilingual retrieval — Grid-search BM25 k,b on a per-language dev set to optimize MRR@100, then test on Mr.TyDi.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if for each evaluated dataset: (a) a grid-search over k × b has grid_size ≥ 9 (e.g., |k| ≥ 3, |b| ≥ 3); (b) the selected (k,b) maximizes dev nDCG@20 and is applied unchanged to test; (c) default-BM25 and tuned-BM25 test nDCG@20 are both reported; (d) dev/test topic overlap == 0. Otherwise fail.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Establishes a strong, tuned lexical baseline per standard practice to avoid weak-baseline confounds.

experiment_recipes.goal: BM25->CEDR reranking on Robust04 with significance
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: BM25 candidate generation then neural reranking — Generate top-k (e.g., k=100–150) candidates with BM25 (or QL) and rerank with neural models; select k on dev; report P@20/nDCG@20/ERR@20.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if: (a) k_selected ∈ {100,150} chosen on a held-out Robust04 dev split; (b) evaluation follows Robust04 5-fold (i.e., number_of_folds == 5) with no cross-fold leakage; (c) for each fold, BM25 (initial) and CEDR (reranked) results are reported for P@20, nDCG@20, ERR@20; (d) paired t-tests across topics are run for CEDR vs BM25 and p-values are reported for all three metrics on the fold-averaged results (i.e., number_of_p_values_reported ≥ 3). Otherwise fail.
depends_on: Tuned BM25 apparatus on BEIR dev/test
experiment_recipes.rationale: Checks the standard BM25-candidate-plus-neural-reranker pipeline with proper fold splits and significance testing.

experiment_recipes.goal: Sparse–Dense hybrid fusion on BEIR with alpha tuning and efficiency reporting
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Sparse–Dense hybrid score fusion — Normalize BM25 and dense scores to [0,1] and combine via s_sparse + α·s_dense; tune α on dev.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if: (a) scores are min–max normalized to [0,1] per dataset; (b) α is tuned on a held-out dev set over a grid of at least 5 values and the argmax is applied unchanged to test; (c) test reports include BM25-only, dense-only, and hybrid under identical candidate pools and identical ANN settings; (d) nDCG@20 and Recall@100 are reported on ≥ 8 BEIR datasets; (e) for each method, Index size (GB) and Latency (ms/query) are measured over ≥ 1000 queries and Processing rate (docs/sec) is reported. Otherwise fail.
depends_on: Zero-shot BEIR after MS MARCO training gate
Tuned BM25 apparatus on BEIR dev/test
experiment_recipes.rationale: Validates hybrid fusion under matched conditions and reports standard effectiveness–efficiency trade-offs.

experiment_recipes.goal: Rank list overlap (RBO) analysis BM25 vs dense vs hybrid
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Rank list overlap analysis — Compute Rank Biased Overlap between methods to assess lexical vs semantic behavior similarities.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if for each of ≥ 8 BEIR datasets: (a) RBO at cutoff 100 is computed for BM25 vs dense and BM25 vs hybrid; (b) the average RBO over queries and its 95% bootstrap CI are reported; (c) the exact same query set and candidate pool are used across methods. Otherwise fail.
depends_on: Sparse–Dense hybrid fusion on BEIR with alpha tuning and efficiency reporting
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ensures lexical vs semantic behavior is analyzed via standard rank-overlap diagnostics.

experiment_recipes.goal: Token-shuffled query stress test for order sensitivity
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Query stress tests — Evaluate on token-shuffled queries to probe order sensitivity and lexical matching behavior.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if for at least 3 BEIR datasets: (a) each original query is token-shuffled (random permutation) without changing tokenization; (b) nDCG@20 is evaluated on original and shuffled queries for BM25-only, dense-only, and hybrid; (c) per-method ΔnDCG@20 = nDCG@20_original − nDCG@20_shuffled is reported; (d) identical indexes and candidate pools are used across original vs shuffled. Otherwise fail.
depends_on: Sparse–Dense hybrid fusion on BEIR with alpha tuning and efficiency reporting
experiment_recipes.rationale: Differentiates lexical term-matching behavior from order-sensitive semantic matching per community stress-test norms.
